options: An independent, isolated geographic AWS deployment, such as us-east-1, that most resources live in exactly one of
A single physical data center building with no further subdivision
A synonym for an Availability Zone — the two terms mean the same thing
A CloudFront caching site used only for content delivery
questions.explain: A Region is a geographic area made up of multiple independent Availability Zones; most resources are created in exactly one Region.

options: One of several physically separate data centers inside a Region, each with its own independent power, cooling, and networking
A backup copy of an entire Region kept in another country
The public-facing name for an AWS data transfer fee tier
A smaller caching site used exclusively by CloudFront
questions.explain: AZs are the isolated data centers a Region is built from — a failure in one shouldn't take down another.

questions.q: Why do production workloads typically get deployed across multiple Availability Zones instead of just one?
options: So a power, cooling, or hardware failure in one AZ doesn't take the whole application down, since another AZ keeps serving traffic
Because AWS requires every account to use at least two AZs by law
Because a single AZ cannot legally host more than one EC2 instance
Because Availability Zones are billed at a lower rate when used in pairs
questions.explain: Spreading across AZs is the core mechanism for isolating a single data center's failure from taking the whole application down.

questions.q: How does an Edge Location differ from a Region or an Availability Zone?
options: It's a smaller, far more numerous site used by services like CloudFront and Route 53 to serve cached content or DNS closer to users — it doesn't run EC2 or most AWS services
It is simply another name for an Availability Zone
It is a Region reserved exclusively for AWS's own internal use
It always contains more Availability Zones than a standard Region
questions.explain: Edge Locations exist purely to shorten the network path to cached content or DNS answers — they are not scaled-down Regions.

questions.q: Why might the Availability Zone labeled `us-east-1a` in one AWS account not be the same physical data center as `us-east-1a` in a different account?
options: AWS randomizes the AZ letter mapping per account to spread load evenly across the real physical AZs, and exposes a stable AZ ID for cases that need consistency
Because AZ letters are reassigned randomly every 24 hours for every account
Because `us-east-1a` doesn't actually correspond to a real data center in any account
Because only paid AWS support tiers get consistent AZ letter mappings
questions.explain: The per-account randomization of AZ letters is why AWS also provides AZ IDs for anything that needs to line up consistently across accounts.
